facebook.deskripsi:
Fires burned nearly 2.9 million hectares of Indonesia between January and October 2026, according to one satellite monitor. In many places, nobody has proven who started them.

This video looks at why drained peat burns, whose concessions had burned ground, what the companies and the palm certification body say, and where enforcement has fallen short. Suspects have not been found guilty, and mapping where it burned does not show how a fire started.

Narration uses a synthetic voice.

items.komentar: Is there drained peatland near where you live? What happens to it in the dry season?

facebook.deskripsi:
Wet peat is hard to light. Canals pull the water out, and the peat dries from the top down. A 2025 study of Sumatra and Borneo found up to thirteen times more fire hotspots per square kilometre on drained peat.

Narration uses a synthetic voice.
